n1.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: Ah - you have come about your grandmother's things?
She kept a notebook, and she always said it was not finished.
It has been sitting in the store room since she stopped travelling. Pages everywhere.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: You matched all six. And her hand is still on the first page.
Then it is settled: the notebook travels again, and you are the one carrying it.
Write down what people tell you. Their words, their names, their places.

n1.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: The loose pages are in the store room - the room is the big house north of the square.
Line them up by what is drawn on them.

n1.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: Packing is the same work as building - it has an order.
Carry water, salt, a little sambal, and something to write with.
The rest you can buy or be given along the way.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: Good. Then you will not be the traveller who arrives empty-handed.
One more thing: take the basket from the mending shed - the village filled it for you.
Cloth, coffee, salt. Gifts. People will ask you where you are from.

n1.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: The shed is west of the square. Bring the basket, and we will pack it together.

n1.speaker: npc_nelayan
lines: You want to go inland? Then you will need this net mended first, and a letter.
The letter says the next village should receive you. The keeper signs those.
Here is the twine. My shuttle is on the bench.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_nelayan
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_nelayan
lines: That is a good mend - better than mine, and I have been doing it forty years.
The keeper signed the letter while you were working. Take it.
Inland, the roads climb. It is cold up there in the morning. Go carefully.

n1.speaker: npc_nelayan
lines: The twine is in your hand already. My bench is at the jetty, west of the houses.

n1.speaker: npc_aminah
lines: You came up the new road? Then you are the traveller with the notebook.
Look at this wall - the panels were taken down to be cleaned and now nobody agrees where they go.
Help me match them and I will tell you about the house.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_aminah
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_aminah
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_aminah
lines: There - exactly. My mother would have put them the same way.
This house belongs to the women of the family, you know. It is theirs, not the men's.
Write that down before you forget it.

n1.speaker: npc_aminah
lines: The panels are stacked against the wall on the east side of the house.

n1.speaker: npc_ida
lines: A wedding across the valley, which means rendang, which means I have been cooking since dawn.
The spice bundle is still at the market stall and the coconut milk is at the grinder.
Bring both, and then you can watch the pot - I need another pair of hands.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_ida
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_ida
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_ida
lines: Nearly dry, and the colour is right. Sit down, you have earned a plate.
Rendang is cooked this dry so it keeps. That is why it travels - and why weddings always have it.

n1.speaker: npc_ida
lines: Everything is in the pot. Watch the fire with me - keep it steady.

n1.speaker: npc_bujang
lines: I cut a new saluang, and then I forgot how the song begins. Imagine!
My teacher used to say the flute breathes for you if you let it.
Take the blank and try. You do not need to be good, you need to listen.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_bujang
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_bujang
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_bujang
lines: That is it. That is the song.
You know what is strange? You cannot get a good breath by breathing in and out normally.
You push the air out while you breathe in through your nose. That is why a phrase can last so long.

n1.speaker: npc_bujang
lines: The blank is with the bamboo clump behind the house. Take it and try a phrase.

n1.speaker: npc_sari
lines: The wedding is tomorrow and the loom is fighting me.
I have the yarn, but the pattern has to be laid out before the thread tangles.
Will you fetch the gold thread from the trader? It is the last thing I need.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_sari
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_sari
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_sari
lines: Good. Now it will hold.
This kind of cloth is not sold in a shop - it is given. At a birth, at a wedding, at a funeral.
Giving one is the same as saying a blessing out loud.

n1.speaker: npc_sari
lines: The loom is under the lean-to. Sit at it and copy the pattern.

n1.speaker: npc_datuak
lines: You have heard the flute and watched the cloth; now comes the music for the procession.
The talempong is a set of small bronze gongs. One person cannot play a whole tune - we strike, and the tune comes out between us.
Learn the pattern, then try the procession game at the square.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_datuak
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_datuak
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_datuak
lines: Enough. The wedding will have its music.
Small gongs like these travel well - we can carry the whole set to the next village. A big bronze orchestra could never do that.

n1.speaker: npc_datuak
lines: Come to the frame of gongs behind the elders' house. I will show you the pattern.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Half my goods went into the lake this morning. Everybody saw it, nobody agrees where.
A boy says the reeds caught it. The cake seller says it went past her stall.
Walk up to the lake and work out where it actually came ashore, would you?

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: My basket, my salt, my coffee - all dry inside.
I have travelled this lake shore for twenty years and I would not have guessed that spot.
You read the shore better than I do. That is worth a sack of beans.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Come up to the lake with me and look at the shore.

n1.speaker: npc_penari
lines: Hold these. Careful - they are real plates, not props.
We dance with them in our palms, and at the end we step on them.
The new dancer keeps starting with the hardest part. Help her sort the order.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_penari
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_penari
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_penari
lines: Now she has it. One more rehearsal and the harvest festival will be ready.
You should know where the dance comes from: it began as a thank-you for the rice harvest.
That is why we still dance it when the field is cut.

n1.speaker: npc_penari
lines: The troupe is north of the square, on the mat. Come and dance one round.

n1.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: Market opens at first light and everything has to be in the right place.
Gold thread, chilli, coffee, cloth, a little bronze - and I keep mixing them up.
Help me sort them and I will tell the boatman that you need the eastern road.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: Open on time. Look at that - the whole street trading.
Take this scarf; it is not the best one I have made, but it is the one I can spare.
The eastern road runs to the coast, then south along the water. Another island is waiting.

n1.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: The stalls are at the eastern end. Bring the goods and we will sort them.

n1.speaker: npc_koki
lines: You are just in time to help, and I am not asking.
Tonight is a syukuran - a thanksgiving - and there has to be tumpeng.
The ingredients are at the market stall. Bring them and stay for the fire.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_koki
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_koki
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_koki
lines: Now that is a mountain, not a lump. The tip goes to the eldest, you know.
We cut the top first and give it away, then everybody eats the rest.
Write that down: the shape is the mountain, and the mountain is what feeds us.

n1.speaker: npc_koki
lines: The stove is behind the warung. Come and help me finish it.

n1.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: Careful, the wax is hot. No - hotter than that. Good.
This cloth will go into the dye bath twice. Whatever the wax covers stays light.
Draw this pattern for me and I will show you why our patterns have names.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: Now look at it against the light. Pale where the wax was, dark where the dye went.
Some patterns are for weddings and some for everyday - it is not only decoration.
That is why we say a batik has a name, not just a design.

n1.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: The cloth is stretched on the frame. Sit down and draw with the pen.

n1.speaker: npc_ki_bagus
lines: Sit here. Do not play yet - listen first.
Each gamelan is tuned to suit itself, so a set is played together or not at all.
We play for the temple anniversary. Keep time with the drum and you will be fine.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_ki_bagus
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_ki_bagus
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_ki_bagus
lines: You kept time, and you did not rush. That is the whole art.
Two tunings: one with five notes to the octave, one with seven. We use one at a time.
Because a set is tuned as a set, you cannot mix instruments from two gamelan. Remember that.

n1.speaker: npc_ki_bagus
lines: The instruments are laid out in the pendopo. Sit at the saron and follow the drum.

n1.speaker: npc_pak_tarno
lines: Every family here takes water in turn - that is how the terraces have survived.
Today the gate jammed and the lowest field is drying.
Go up the terrace path and open the channels again, then bring seedlings down.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_pak_tarno
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_pak_tarno
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_pak_tarno
lines: Water is running to the lowest field. Good. Nobody's crop will fail today.
You saw how the channels are shared? No single household owns that water.
We keep the schedule together, and everyone eats. That is the whole system.

n1.speaker: npc_pak_tarno
lines: The gate is up on the terrace path. Turn the channels until the water reaches the field.

n1.speaker: npc_mbah_karto
lines: My eyes are tired, and my hands are still steady. It is the remembering that goes first.
Tonight I need someone who can answer questions in front of the village.
The story note is at the workshop. Bring it, and answer what I ask.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_mbah_karto
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_mbah_karto

n1.speaker: npc_mbah_karto
lines: Correct, all three. Tonight you sit beside the screen and watch the shadows.
The puppets are flat leather, and every one of them has a voice - the dalang gives it to them.
That is what people come to hear: one person, a hundred voices, until morning.

n1.speaker: npc_mbah_karto
lines: Sit here. I will ask the questions the way the village asks them.

n1.speaker: npc_rara
lines: You cannot play angklung alone. That is the point of it.
Each of these makes one note or one chord, so the tune is spread across thirty children.
Help me teach them the order, then join the group game at the square.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

no.speaker: npc_rara

lines: Listen to them! Nobody is playing fast, and it works.
This is how it is taught in school here - in a group, never in a practice room alone.
One instrument, one note, everybody needed.

n1.speaker: npc_rara
lines: The children are on the square with the instruments. Show them the order first.

n1.speaker: npc_dewi
lines: Careful - do not touch the carvings, just look. We are copying, not restoring.
The temple is built as a stepped mountain: you climb through galleries before the open terraces.
Someone turned the panel blocks to clean behind them, and now the row is wrong.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

no.speaker: npc_dewi

lines: The row is right again. Thank you.
People walk it clockwise. Each level is a stage, and the reliefs are read as you climb.
It was built in the eighth century, and it is still the largest Buddhist temple anywhere.

n1.speaker: npc_dewi
lines: Meet me at the temple grounds on the eastern road. Bring steady hands.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Half past five and the stalls already disagree about where they belong.
Sort them for me? Rice, wax, mallets, seedlings, a fan - simple enough.
Then I will tell you which road goes south to the river ports.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Open, and trading. Take this square of batik; the maker owes me a favour.
South of here the road reaches the river country. Rivers, not roads, are the way in.
Look for the long houses. You will know them when you see them.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: The market is on the square right now - come and help me sort it.

n1.speaker: npc_lasan
lines: You came up the river? Then you have seen the house from the water - one long roof, the whole village under it.
The storm took four panels off the gallery. We weave the replacements by hand.
Help me finish one and then walk the gallery. It is longer than you think.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_lasan
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_lasan
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_lasan
lines: Good panel. That will hold the rain off for ten years.
Every family has its own rooms along the gallery - and the gallery itself belongs to everyone.
That is why we repair it together and nobody argues about whose roof it is.

n1.speaker: npc_lasan
lines: The rattan is soaking behind the house. Come and plait a panel with me.

n1.speaker: npc_tina
lines: Listen. Do you hear how the words sit on the beat? Not on top of it - on it.
My grandmother could sing a story for an hour without losing the thread.
Help me keep the pulse through a whole verse. The drum will show you.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_tina
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_tina

n1.speaker: npc_tina
lines: You held it. Now you know why the stories survive: the tune remembers the words for you.
Advice, praise, the history of a place - all of it arrives singing.
Write down what she told you, if you can. Words like that should not be lost.

n1.speaker: npc_tina
lines: Sit with me on the gallery. The drum is here - keep the pulse with it.

n1.speaker: npc_bapa_udi
lines: Rivers are our roads, and today our road is blocked. A tree came down in the night.
Turn the channel pieces until the current runs to the landing again.
Mind the bank - the mud goes deeper than your boots.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_bapa_udi
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_bapa_udi

n1.speaker: npc_bapa_udi
lines: Boat coming in already. Listen to that engine.
In the dry season the water drops and the channels change. We read the water the way you read a road sign.
Come back in the wet season and the whole map will be different.

n1.speaker: npc_bapa_udi
lines: Bring the boat up with me. The channel pieces are on the bank.

n1.speaker: npc_rini
lines: Everything is tied, dyed and hung up - and the pattern is once again a mess.
When the ties are placed at random you get a muddy cloth.
Watch where I tie mine, then copy it. The thread is with the trader at the landing.

choices.text: I will help.

n1.speaker: npc_rini
lines: That is the pattern. Now look at the cloth after the dye has done its work.
We call it sasirangan. The ties stay light, the rest goes deep.
It used to be for ceremonies only. Now people wear it every day, and that is fine too.

n1.speaker: npc_rini
lines: The dye pot is on the veranda. Watch the ties, then copy them.

n1.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: The bench went over in the night. Every tool is out of its place.
A good blade is not sold in a market here - it is made, sharpened and passed down.
Pair them up for me and I will show you the one I use every day.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_pengrajin

n1.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: There. The blade is for clearing brush, splitting rattan and cutting timber.
The little knife on the sheath is the one that actually does the fine work.
It goes to a funeral dressed as well, but that is not what makes it valuable. The work does.

n1.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: Everything is piled on the bench. Start with the blade and its sheath.

n1.speaker: npc_koki
lines: Boats start arriving before dawn and they expect soup.
Cinnamon, star anise, clove - whole, not ground. That is what makes the smell.
Come and help, and then we will take a bowl to the floating market.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_koki
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_koki

n1.speaker: npc_koki
lines: Drink it. That is the flavour of a river port: spices that came by ship, beef from upriver, peanut from the market.
Every ingredient here has travelled further than you have. Remember that when you eat.

n1.speaker: npc_koki
lines: The pot is on the stove at the stall. Come and taste as we go.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: I bought salt, and now three boatmen each swear somebody else has it.
Boat A carries fruit. B is at the far end. C is moored next to the one with my salt.
Work it out for me - I am too old to interrogate three liars before breakfast.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Boat C. Of course it is C.
You would be a good market trader. Haggling is mostly noticing things.
Take these; there is nothing in this life you cannot learn by watching a landing.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Come down to the landing and listen to them argue.

n1.speaker: npc_penari
lines: We dance the planting before we plant - it is a rehearsal for the fields.
The bamboo pole is the dibble stick, and the seed is real seed.
Help me get the order right, then dance one round with us.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_penari

no.speaker: npc_penari

n1.speaker: npc_penari
lines: That is the whole cycle, danced in four minutes.
The stick makes the hole, the hand drops the seed, the foot closes it. Then wait for rain.
Take this, and take the northern road when you are ready. The sea is past the hills.

n1.speaker: npc_penari
lines: The dancers are on the long jetty. Bring seed and we will rehearse.

n1.speaker: npc_puang
lines: Do not touch the old carvings - only the new panels above the door need turning.
The house itself has been in the family for generations; the gable, we renew.
Help me line them up and then stand in front of the house. You should see it properly.

choices.text: I will help.

yes.speaker: npc_puang

no.speaker: npc_puang

n1.speaker: npc_puang
lines: Straight and level. The house looks as it should again.
The building belongs to the family line, not to one person. That is why we all work on it, and why the heirlooms are kept inside it.
Now look up at the roof - it sweeps to a point at both ends, like a saddle.

n1.speaker: npc_puang
lines: The panels are on the veranda of the house. Come and help me turn them.

n1.speaker: npc_dg_naba
lines: She will be two masts and about twenty metres. Not one nail in her.

Check my layout before we peg it - once the pegs are in, the shape is decided.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

n1.speaker: npc_dg_naba
lines: That will hold. When the tide is high we will roll her down the beach and she will float.
No paper drawings - the shape lives in the builder's head and the hands of the crew.
That is why the knowledge is not written anywhere. It is passed from master to apprentice.

n1.speaker: npc_dg_naba
lines: The hull frame is on the beach. Bring the planking and check my layout.

n1.speaker: npc_rambu
lines: A wedding needs music and our group is one short.
Each of us covers a voice - melody, middle, bass. It only works as a group.
Learn this pattern and you can stand in with us.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_rambu

n1.speaker: npc_rambu
lines: You will do. Play like that at the wedding and nobody will notice you are new.
The bars are wooden, and the mallets are padded so the note rings instead of clattering.
One set, three voices, played by three people. Just like the angklung, but with wood.

n1.speaker: npc_rambu
lines: The frame is set up behind the house. Stand at the bars and copy me.

n1.speaker: npc_koki
lines: Boat workers want one thing: soup they can eat standing up.
The beef has been simmering since before dawn. Now the spice mix, then the peanut.
The mix is at the spice stall by the harbour gate. Bring it, then stay and stir.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_koki

no.speaker: npc_koki

n1.speaker: npc_koki
lines: That is it. Eat a bowl and go look at the ships - the same water carried the spices here.
Coriander and cumin did not grow on this island. They came by sea, and stayed.
Every dish you have eaten on this journey is a record of a journey somebody else made.

n1.speaker: npc_koki
lines: The pot is at the harbour stall. Bring the spice mix and we will finish it.

lines: The new ones keep accelerating. You cannot hurry this dance.

Try it with me - follow the drum and do not count.

n1.speaker: npc_penari
lines: That was calm. That is what the dance is for: it tells a guest that nobody is in a hurry.
Small steps, fan in hand, eyes up. Nothing is meant to look difficult.
Harder than it looks, yes. That is the point of it.

n1.speaker: npc_penari
lines: We rehearse in the yard by the harbour. Stand at the back and follow the drum.

n1.speaker: npc_guru
lines: These are old records, written on palm leaf strips. Genealogy, law, diary, land.
The labels rotted away, so we have to work them out again.
One of them I cannot place. Read the marks and the lengths and tell me what it is.

n1.speaker: npc_guru
lines: The land record. That settles it - the boundary notes match what the elders remember.
The script came from India long ago and was written on palm leaf with a sharp point.
A written record is how a community argues with itself without losing the memory.

n1.speaker: npc_guru
lines: The strips are on the table in the archive. Look at them with me.

n1.speaker: npc_nelayan
lines: Two mornings, empty nets. The children will eat sago and we will eat sago.
Everyone saw something different. One saw the shallows near the walkway, another saw the reef edge, another the channel.
Put it together for me - where should we go at first light?

n1.speaker: npc_nelayan
lines: There. That is where we will be at first light.
How did you work it? The shallows are close to the walkway, the reef meets the channel, and north of the channel is where the fish school.
You think like a fisher now. Take this shell, and this sash - for luck.

n1.speaker: npc_nelayan
lines: Come out to the walkway with me. Bring the reports.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: The eastern boat leaves at high tide and I still have to close the ledger.
Silk, ships, palm-leaf records, sago, coffee - five cargoes, five places.
Match them for me and I will get you a place on the boat.

choices.text: I will help.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Ledger closed. The boat is at the end of the pier, sails already up.
East of here the mountains get higher and the languages get more numerous.
Go carefully, ask before you write, and take your time.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: The ledger is on the table at the end of the pier.

n1.speaker: npc_yosia
lines: You came up from the coast? Then you felt how cold the night is here.
These houses are round, with a roof of thatch that comes almost to the ground.
The door is low, so you go in bowing. It keeps the heat in and the wind out.

n1.speaker: npc_yosia
lines: Done. Now sit by the fire until your hands work again.
The hearth sits in the middle of the floor and the smoke finds its way out through the thatch.
Cold outside, warm inside. Everything about the shape is for that.

n1.speaker: npc_yosia
lines: The thatch is stacked beside the house. Come up and copy the shape.

n1.speaker: npc_mama_lena
lines: The bag is not sewn and not woven on a loom. It is knotted.
Pull it and it stretches; put a baby in it and it holds. That is the whole design.
Bring the fibre and pair the knots with me - I have forgotten two of them.

n1.speaker: npc_mama_lena
lines: Both right. Now the bag will hang straight on your back.
You can carry sweet potato, firewood, or a baby in it, and it hangs from your head, so your hands stay free.
People have used these here for a very long time. It is not a small thing.

n1.speaker: npc_mama_lena
lines: The fibre is on the rack. Sit with me and pair the knots.

n1.speaker: npc_petrus
lines: You are hungry, so you are useful. Sit and stir.
This is papeda: sago starch stirred into boiling water until it turns clear.
The fish soup goes with it - yellow with turmeric, sour with lime.

n1.speaker: npc_petrus
lines: Wrap it round the fork, dip it in the soup, and swallow. Do not chew, it does not need chewing.
Sago comes from a palm that grows in wet ground where rice will not.
So the food changes with the land. Rice where there are fields, sago where there is swamp.

n1.speaker: npc_petrus
lines: The pot is on the fire. Bring the sago and the fish and stir.

n1.speaker: npc_tomas
lines: The drum carries the beat for everything - singing, dancing, calling people in.
You play sitting, with the drum on your lap or the ground, one hand on the skin.
Watch my call and answer it back to me.

n1.speaker: npc_tomas
lines: That is the call. Tonight they will hear it from the other side of the valley.
This drum is carved from one piece of wood, and the skin is scraped thin and stretched.
A good drum is loud without shouting. Take this small one - it is quiet, but it is a start.

n1.speaker: npc_tomas
lines: The drum is with me by the house. Watch, then answer.

n1.speaker: npc_guru
lines: In the highlands the ground is wet, but the water still has to move or the roots rot.
So we dig ditches, not walls. That is different from the rice fields you saw on Java.
Help me show the children where the water should run.

lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_guru
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_guru
lines: Now the beds are moist and not drowned. The children have seen why the ditch is there.
The gardens here grow sweet potato, taro and yam - heavy crops, for a cold place.
Different island, different field, different answer. All three work.

n1.speaker: npc_guru
lines: The ditches run behind the school. Bring the children - and turn the channels.

n1.speaker: npc_petrus
lines: The canoe drifted in the night. Nobody is hurt - it is the canoe we are missing.
Four people saw it, four different directions.
Take their words to the lakeshore and work out where it actually ended up.

choices.text: I will help.

n1.speaker: npc_petrus
lines: It is there, tied up by the racks. The children will row it back tomorrow.
Four witnesses, four directions, and all four were partly right. That is how talk works.
Write down who saw what, not only what was true. Your notebook will be better for it.

n1.speaker: npc_petrus
lines: The lake is east of the village. Take the directions with you.

n1.speaker: npc_mama_lena
lines: Cloth from bark. Not from a plant stem, not from an animal - from the inside of a tree.
You strip it, soak it, and beat it until it spreads. Then you wait for it to dry.
Tell me the order, then beat it with me.

n1.speaker: npc_mama_lena
lines: Flat, soft and pale. Now it can be painted.
Patterns belong to families here. What I paint, I was given the right to paint.
That is why I will not copy somebody else's design onto it, and neither should you.

n1.speaker: npc_mama_lena
lines: The bark is soaking behind the house. Bring the mallet.

n1.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: I have walked up here for eleven mornings and seen almost nothing. That is bird watching.
This morning: a display at first light, plumes up over the head, near the ridge.
My handwriting in the dark is unreadable. Read it back to me.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: Then come back when you are ready - it will keep.

n1.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: The dawn bird, then. And nobody touched it, nobody caged it, nobody chased it.
These birds were hunted almost to nothing for their feathers once - sold far away as decoration.
Now they are protected here and by international trade rules. That is why we watch with our eyes only.

n2.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: One more thing. Pak Hasan in Kampung Awal has been asking when you are coming home. Whatever that test of his is, I would go and take it.

n1.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: Come up to the ridge with me at first light and read the notes.

n1.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: Sit. The notebook is nearly full, so there is one thing left to do.
I will ask, and you will answer, and then we will both know what you actually learned.
Do not worry about the score. Nobody has ever failed this by being honest.

choices.text: I will help.
Not yet, but I will come back.

yes.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: Good. Take your time, and write down what you learn.

no.speaker: npc_penjaga

n1.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: Every answer right. Then close it and look at what you have written.
You started with your grandmother's half-filled notebook. Now look at it.
One more thing, outside. The whole village is waiting.

n1.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: Sit here. We will do the questions one at a time.

n1.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: Stand here. Look around you for a moment.
There are people in this square from six islands. Nobody planned that; they came because you wrote to them.

n2.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: Your grandmother wrote one line on the first page and left it at that.
It says: it is not one culture, and it is not a hundred separate ones.
It is people who trade, borrow, argue and celebrate together across the water.

n3.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: She never finished the sentence. You have.
The notebook is closed. The islands are open. Go and look at them again - there is no hurry now.
And if somebody asks you what Indonesia is, hand them the notebook.

n1.speaker: npc_aminah
lines: The house is old, but the wall was renewed twice. Nothing here is frozen.
If you sit on the veranda long enough, somebody always comes by with news.

n1.speaker: npc_datuak
lines: Bronze gongs like ours are carried to the wedding in a basket - front and back, like a boat.
When you write down what we say, write our names beside it. Then people will know who spoke.

n1.speaker: npc_sari
lines: A backstrap loom can only make cloth as wide as my arms are long. That is why our cloths are narrow.
Red, black and white. Those are the colours you will see on a woman's cloth at a wedding.

n1.speaker: npc_bujang
lines: Listen - that is the wind in the bamboo, not music. It is a good day when the two agree.
A flute is cheap to make and impossible to make well. Cut one yourself and you will see.

n1.speaker: npc_ida
lines: Everything here starts with coconut. Milk, oil, sugar - the same tree, three different things.
Eat with your right hand if you are eating with your hand. And wash first, always.

n1.speaker: npc_ki_bagus
lines: Sit anywhere you like. The instruments do not belong to anyone in particular except the set.
You can hear the difference between two gamelans in a single note. Each set finds its own pitch.

n1.speaker: npc_dewi
lines: We do not restore the reliefs. We copy them, and we write down what condition they are in.
The stone has been repaired more than once, and each repair is part of the building's history.

n1.speaker: npc_pak_tarno
lines: Rice will stand in water for weeks and then want to be dry for cutting. Two moods, one plant.
The ducks come after the harvest, and they eat what we would have to clear. That is the trade.

n1.speaker: npc_rara
lines: Thirty children, thirty instruments, one tune. It is the easiest lesson and the hardest.
One tube per note. Nothing here is decoration - the length of the tube makes the pitch.

n1.speaker: npc_mbah_karto
lines: A performance can run to morning. I have fallen asleep twice, and both times the puppets survived.
The stories are old, but the jokes are new every night. That is how the crowd stays.

n1.speaker: npc_lasan
lines: The gallery belongs to everyone, so we repair it together and nobody writes down who paid.
Up here the roof is our biggest worry. Down at the coast their worry is the tide.

n1.speaker: npc_tina
lines: A sung story can carry advice, praise or grief. The tune decides how far the words travel.
My grandmother sang for an hour without repeating herself. I manage four verses.

n1.speaker: npc_bapa_udi
lines: In the wet season the river takes the road. Then we travel on the water and forget the road exists.
Never swim after rain. The current under a brown surface is not what it looks like from the bank.

n1.speaker: npc_rini
lines: Tie it tight and it stays light. Tie it loose and the dye creeps in. That is the whole pattern.
Combed cotton came here by trade. Our own fibre is bark and rattan, and that goes the other way.

n1.speaker: npc_rambu
lines: Wooden bars, padded sticks, three players. The bass player is the one who never seems busy.
In the villages here, the music group is also the church choir. Same people, different chairs.

n1.speaker: npc_puang
lines: The house is not mine. It belongs to the line - I merely keep the door open.
When the family gathers, we sleep on the gallery and the grandchildren go to the rice store.

n1.speaker: npc_dg_naba
lines: I do not draw hulls. I have built twelve, and the thirteenth will be slightly better than the twelfth.
The timber is bought three years before it is cut. Wet wood fights the builder.

n1.speaker: npc_yuliana
lines: In the highlands the soil is thin and the rain is heavy. We plant along the slope, not across it.
Nutmeg, clove, coconut - a garden here is also a spice shop.

n1.speaker: npc_yosia
lines: The roof has to be three fingers thick or the rain finds a way through.
We build in a circle here. In the villages down at the coast, the houses are long and rectangular.

n1.speaker: npc_petrus
lines: The lake is calm in the morning and dishonest in the afternoon. Cross early.
A canoe has a name and a family. If it is gone, we know who to ask first.

n1.speaker: npc_mama_lena
lines: Pull the knot tight and the bag stretches. It hangs from my head, so my hands stay free.
I do not sell other families' patterns. What I make, I was given the right to make.

n1.speaker: npc_tomas
lines: One piece of wood, one skin. If the wood has a crack in it, the drum will always answer badly.
You play sitting down. Standing up turns a drum into a noise.

n1.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: A village keeps records in three ways: in writing, in what people remember, and in the ground.
Ask before you write. Nobody minds a notebook that asks first.

n1.speaker: npc_pengembara
lines: I have walked from the eastern islands to the western ones. Twice, in fact. My knees are not friends with me.
Carry less than you think, and something to give away. That is the whole of travelling.

n1.speaker: npc_anak
lines: Did you see the boat? It had a red sail! I saw it first!
My cousin says there are islands that are all mountains. Is that true?

n1.speaker: npc_nelayan
lines: The tide here runs hard on the full moon. Everybody plans around that, not around the clock.
Mend the net before it tears. A mend costs an hour; a tear costs a morning.

lines: Take a look. Prices are in Culture Points - that is how we count favours on this journey.

n1.speaker: npc_guru
lines: There are over seven hundred languages in this country. Every one of them carries something.
A class of thirty children here may speak two languages at home. That is not a problem, it is a library.

n1.speaker: npc_penari
lines: Dance first, then talk. The body explains it faster than I can.
Every region's dance is built differently because the story it tells is different.

n1.speaker: npc_pengrajin
lines: A good craftsperson is a good listener. The material tells you what it wants to become.
If I cannot make it twice, I have not finished learning it.

lines: Take a look. Prices are in Culture Points - that is how we count favours on this journey.

n1.speaker: npc_koki
lines: A recipe is not a set of instructions. It is a description of the last time somebody made it.
Serve from the outside in, always. The middle of the platter is for sharing.

choices.text: What do you have for sale?

shop.speaker: npc_koki
lines: Take a look. Prices are in Culture Points - that is how we count favours on this journey.

n1.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Prices change with the tide, the harvest and the week. I write them down, which is the only advantage I have.
Everything sells twice: once at the market, once as a story about where it came from.

choices.text: What do you have for sale?
Just passing by.

shop.speaker: npc_pedagang
lines: Take a look. Prices are in Culture Points - that is how we count favours on this journey.

n1.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: You made it up the coast road. Good - the wind was against you all morning.
This is Kampung Awal. One street, one jetty, and my store room full of other people's memories.

n2.speaker: npc_penjaga
lines: Your grandmother left something with me years ago. A notebook, cloth bound, half empty.
Come and talk to me by the well and we will go and find it.
Walk with W A S D or the arrow keys. Press E to talk to people and to look at things. M opens the map, I your bag, J your journal, ESC the menu.
